objective: Audit true slope coverage and calibrate SG042's finite sample HAC uncertainty intervals, explicitly accounting for uncertainty versus decision cost.
algorithm: For each complete 240-sample continuation, group into 24 consecutive 10-point medians, compute centered OLS slope, Newey-West HAC lag 3 SE. Original nominal 90% interval uses z=1.645. Corrected interval uses split-calibration empirical 90th percentile of abs(estimate-true_slope)/SE.

calibration.quantile_rank: ceil((n+1)*0.90) among sorted absolute standardized errors
calibration.note: Calibration contains known synthetic programmed slopes; use truth only in calibration/evaluation, never as input to decisions.

decision_rule: On full 240 acquired observations, confirm drift if interval excludes 0, else reject if entire interval inside ±0.0032, else unresolved. 0.06 units per sample; false confirmation 150, false rejection 90, unresolved 18. This rule is evaluated independently of SG041's early stopping: it is an interval coverage/isolation experiment, not a claim of directly improving the full SG041 controller.
report: Overall and per-scenario empirical slope coverage
All missed-coverage seeds and true slopes
Distinguish marginal exchangeable guarantee from conditional/per-regime coverage
limitations: Conformal rank gives marginal coverage under exchangeability; pooled synthetic regimes and shifts can violate the assumption.
Same generative families in calibration and holdout, new deterministic seeds only.
HAC intervals using short bins are approximations; rank calibration does not establish valid per-regime probability bounds.
Different decision rule than SG042's gate over SG041, so SG042 end-to-end scores are not directly comparable.
